raw_findings.message: A non-integer token makes `parse::<i32>().unwrap()` panic instead of returning an input error, so malformed matrix files crash the process.
Rows shorter than the first row leave `data` smaller than the declared dimensions and can make later operations panic, while longer rows are silently truncated.
The row offset uses `self.rows` instead of `self.cols`, so column totals for rectangular matrices are wrong or panic when the computed index is out of bounds.
Summing valid `i32` cells into an `i32` can overflow, causing a panic in debug builds or an incorrect mean in release builds.
An empty input produces a zero-cell matrix, so calling `mean` divides by zero and panics.
Multiplying a cell by the scale factor can overflow `i32`, causing a panic in debug builds or wrapped, incorrect output in release builds.
Allocating and iterating over `self.cols - 1` omits the final input column from every transpose, and underflows for an empty matrix.
A singular 2x2 matrix has a zero determinant, but the code divides by it and returns infinities or NaNs instead of reporting that no inverse exists.
Writing to a predictable path in `/tmp` follows an existing symlink, allowing a local attacker to make the program overwrite another file writable by its user.
The label and output path are interpolated into a shell command without escaping, so crafted `--label` or `--out` values can execute arbitrary commands.
Unwrapping `load_matrix` makes a missing or unreadable input file panic instead of producing the error returned by the loader.
Casting the accepted `u32` factor to `i32` turns values above `i32::MAX` into negative factors, so valid positive CLI values scale the matrix incorrectly.

raw_findings.message: A non-integer cell makes `parse::<i32>().unwrap()` panic, so malformed input terminates the process instead of returning an error.
Rows are neither checked for consistent width nor rejected when too long, so short rows can leave too little data and later cause panics while extra cells are silently discarded.
The row stride uses `self.rows` instead of `self.cols`, so accessing cells in a non-square matrix returns incorrect values or can index past the data.
Summing matrix values into `i32` can overflow for valid large values, causing a debug-build panic or an incorrect wrapped mean in release builds.
An empty input produces a 0-by-0 matrix, making `mean` divide by zero and panic.
Scaling values can overflow `i32`, causing a debug-build panic or incorrect wrapped results in release builds.
Using `cols - 1` for the output size drops the final input column during transpose, and an input with zero columns underflows.
A singular 2-by-2 matrix has a zero determinant, so inversion returns infinities or NaNs instead of reporting that the matrix cannot be inverted.
Writing to a predictable path in `/tmp` follows an existing symlink, allowing another local user to make the program overwrite a file the program can access.
The user-controlled label and output path are interpolated into a shell command, so crafted `--label` or `--out` values can execute arbitrary commands.
Matrix operations unwrap `load_matrix` errors, so a missing or unreadable input file terminates the process with a panic instead of reporting the error.
Casting the parsed `u32` factor to `i32` wraps values above `i32::MAX` into negative factors, so valid CLI values produce incorrectly scaled results.

Summing enough large cell values can overflow the `i64` mean numerator, causing a panic in debug builds or an incorrect wrapped mean in release builds.

raw_findings.message: A non-integer cell makes `parse::<i32>().unwrap()` panic, so malformed matrix input terminates the process instead of returning an error.
Rows with too few cells are appended without padding and rows with too many are silently truncated, causing malformed matrices to produce incorrect results or panic when accessed.
The row stride uses `self.rows` instead of `self.cols`, so accessing a non-square matrix returns incorrect cells or indexes out of bounds.
Summing cells into `i32` overflows for sufficiently large values, causing a panic in debug builds or an incorrect mean in release builds.
An empty matrix has zero rows and columns, so calling `mean` divides by zero and panics.
Multiplying a cell by the scale factor can exceed the `i32` range, causing a panic in debug builds or wrapped, incorrect output in release builds.
The transpose allocates and iterates over `cols - 1`, dropping the final input column and reporting incorrect dimensions; a zero-column matrix also underflows.
A singular 2x2 matrix has a zero determinant, so inversion returns infinities or NaNs instead of rejecting the matrix.
Writing to a fixed path in `/tmp` follows an attacker-precreated symlink and can overwrite a file writable by the program's user.
Interpolating the user-controlled label and output path into a shell command lets crafted `--label` or `--out` values execute arbitrary commands.
An invalid `--factor` value silently becomes 1, so the scale operation succeeds with a different factor than the user supplied.
Matrix operations unwrap `load_matrix` errors, so a missing or unreadable input file causes a panic instead of a handled error.
A factor above `i32::MAX` wraps when cast to `i32`, so scaling uses a negative or otherwise incorrect factor.
